surfaces.part: rock cliff face (grey stone wall with cracks)
dark chasm void with blue-grey speckle and green growth at the bottom

answer.evidence: The sprite is a full-width 16x64 vertical stone cliff texture. Rows 0-45 are a flat grey wall with crack lines and no band ending in a front-edge line, no eave shadow, no ellipse and no roof plane. Row 0 is only a dark outline, and the rows around 13-19 are crack lines, not an edge. Rows 46-63 fade into a dark void with green growth, which is more vertical face. There is no horizontal top surface anywhere, so this is a front elevation. It also reads as terrain, not a gate, pavilion or building.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a narrow cliff or chasm face strip of grey stone with dark cracks and a small dark plant clump at the bottom. It is not a building, so it has no roof, wall or door structure to compare with the references. Measured facts: 9 visible tones per tile against 12 and 10 for the references, which is slightly lower. Near-flat coverage is 0%, so there are no flat fills, and the stone does carry some mottling. 90% of its dark edge pixels are near-neutral, against 7% and 9% for the references. Its dark crack and edge lines read as neutral black/grey rather than a darkened tint of the adjacent stone, which is the sticker-like outline the references avoid. Its main grey ramp shows about 4 steps against the references' 5-6, and the stones are not shaded one by one with per-stone highlights as in the stone house. Because of the neutral outlines and the shallower shading, it would look flatter than the references beside them.
